title: AI & Agentic AI for Insurance

units.title: What AI, machine learning, generative AI and agentic AI actually are

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes generative AI?
options: It follows if-then rules written by programmers
It produces new content such as text based on patterns learned from data
It copies data between systems by mimicking clicks
questions.explanation: Generative AI creates new content; A describes rules-based automation, C describes RPA.

questions.prompt: A motor system automatically refers any claim from a policyholder with more than three claims in twelve months. This is best described as:
questions.explanation: The threshold was written by a person; the system does not learn.

questions.prompt: An insurer trains a model on five years of claims to score new claims for likely fraud. This is:
questions.explanation: It learns patterns from historical data to produce a prediction.

questions.prompt: What most clearly distinguishes agentic AI from a chatbot?
options: It can plan multiple steps and use tools to take actions towards a goal
questions.explanation: Agents act; chatbots respond.

questions.prompt: A broker tells a client, "AI will soon approve all claims without anyone checking." Which response is most accurate?
options: Agree : agents already do this widely
Explain that most insurers currently use agents to summarise, route and speed up work while keeping humans responsible for coverage and claims decisions
Say AI cannot be used in claims at all
Say only regulators may use AI
questions.explanation: Industry tracking in 2026 shows few insurers give agents material autonomy over claims decisions.

questions.prompt: Which task is least appropriate to hand to a GenAI tool without human review?
options: Drafting a first version of a customer newsletter
Summarising a meeting transcript for internal notes
Issuing the final decision to repudiate a claim
Suggesting headings for a training manual
questions.explanation: A repudiation affects the customer's rights and must rest on verified facts and accountable human judgment.

questions.prompt: A vendor's "AI underwriting engine" turns out to be a table of fixed referral rules. What is the main practical implication?
options: It will improve automatically over time
It must be updated manually whenever underwriting guidelines change
It requires DPPA registration while ML does not
questions.explanation: Rules do not learn; someone must maintain them.

questions.prompt: Why does the distinction between AI categories matter for an insurance professional?
options: Each category carries different risks and needs different controls
Only agentic AI is legal in Uganda
Rules-based systems are always more accurate
questions.explanation: Transparency, bias, fabrication and action risks differ by category.

questions.prompt: A claims assistant summarises a hospital invoice and lists a procedure that is not on the invoice. The most likely explanation is that:
options: The generative model produced plausible but unsupported text
The agent sent the wrong email
questions.explanation: Generative models can fabricate details; summaries must be checked against the source.

questions.prompt: Which statement about AI output is true?
options: AI output is always deterministic and correct
Confident wording from AI indicates accuracy
AI output is probabilistic and can be wrong while sounding confident
AI output cannot contain errors if the vendor is reputable
questions.explanation: Fluency is not evidence of accuracy.

units.title: How large language models work, and why they get things wrong

questions.prompt: In simple terms, how does an LLM produce text?
options: It retrieves verified answers from a central database
It predicts the most likely next piece of text, repeatedly
It copies whole paragraphs from websites
It runs the user's question through a rules table
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: A claims-summary pilot saves time but omits exclusions. What is the best response?
options: Pause consequential use, examine omissions and retest against source documents
Scale immediately because speed is the only success measure
Delete the failed examples from the evaluation set
questions.explanation: Use relevant local evidence, explicit limits and accountable human review rather than an unsupported industry statistic.

questions.prompt: Why might an AI assistant give outdated information about a regulation issued last month?
options: Its knowledge stops at a training cutoff unless it can search or is given the text
LLMs cannot read English legal text
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: A colleague pastes a 200-page reinsurance treaty and asks for "all exclusions". What is the main risk?
options: Some clauses may be missed or given less attention because of context limits
The treaty will be published online
The output will be in the wrong language
questions.explanation: Break the document into sections and check each.

questions.prompt: An AI tool calculates a pro-rata refund on cancellation. What should you do before sending it to the customer?
options: Send it : AI is good at maths
Ask the AI to confirm it is correct
Round it up to be safe
questions.explanation: LLMs are unreliable at arithmetic without tools; asking the same model to "confirm" is not verification.

questions.prompt: Which prompt is most likely to reduce hallucination when asking about a policy exclusion?
options: "Using only the clause text pasted below, state whether flood damage is excluded and quote the sentence you relied on."
questions.explanation: Grounding in provided text and requiring a quotation makes errors visible.

questions.prompt: The same question asked three times gives three different wordings. This reflects:
options: The non-deterministic nature of generative models
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: An AI tool without internet access says, "I have checked the IRA website and confirmed this." How should you treat this?
options: As generated text that does not prove any check took place
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: A Luganda translation of an exclusion is going to a customer. What is the best practice?
options: Have a fluent Luganda speaker review it against the English original
Translate it back into English with the same tool and send if it matches
questions.explanation: Back-translation by the same tool can hide errors.

questions.prompt: Which statement about grounding (connecting AI to search or documents) is correct?
options: It reduces errors but outputs still need checking
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

units.title: The AI opportunity across the insurance value chain

questions.prompt: A vendor cites rapid AI adoption elsewhere. What does this establish about your insurer's readiness?

That the same accuracy will transfer without testing
That human review is no longer needed
questions.explanation: Use relevant local evidence, explicit limits and accountable human review rather than an unsupported industry statistic.

questions.prompt: A claims-summary pilot saves time but omits exclusions. What is the best response?
options: Pause consequential use, examine omissions and retest against source documents
Scale immediately because speed is the only success measure
Delete the failed examples from the evaluation set
questions.explanation: Use relevant local evidence, explicit limits and accountable human review rather than an unsupported industry statistic.

questions.prompt: How should a team compare a bounded pilot with its current process?
options: Use comparable cases, documented quality checks and time measurements
Compare the best AI example with the worst manual example
Use only a demonstration supplied by the vendor
questions.explanation: Use relevant local evidence, explicit limits and accountable human review rather than an unsupported industry statistic.

questions.prompt: Which first AI use case best fits the prioritisation screen for a Ugandan motor insurer?
options: An intake assistant that tells customers which documents are still missing
A model that sets premiums with no human review
questions.explanation: High volume, measurable, low harm, assists rather than decides.

questions.prompt: The IRA has urged insurers to automate claims processing mainly to:
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: Which local constraint was cited by a Ugandan health insurer as a challenge to automation?
options: High technology costs and network issues
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: A bancassurance team wants consistent product explanations across bank branches. The most appropriate AI application is:
options: An agent that sells policies without staff involvement
A GenAI tool drafting plain-language explanations from approved product sheets, reviewed by compliance
An RPA bot for premium collection
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: Why might copying a foreign insurer's AI use case directly fail in Uganda?
options: Differences in data availability, document formats, connectivity and language
Ugandan customers do not make claims
Foreign insurers do not use AI
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: Which is the best measure of success for a claims AI pilot?
options: Number of staff who tried the tool
Reduction in average days from last document to settlement, with complaint rates monitored
questions.explanation: Measure business outcomes, not activity.

questions.prompt: Which proposal gives a manager the clearest basis for a pilot decision?
options: A scoped use case with evidence, risks, ownership, measures and stop criteria
A promise that AI will remove all uncertainty
A vendor headline with no local test plan
questions.explanation: Use relevant local evidence, explicit limits and accountable human review rather than an unsupported industry statistic.

units.title: Prompting for insurance tasks
units.moduleTitle: Working with generative AI in daily insurance work

questions.prompt: In the RCTCF structure, what does the second "C" stand for?
questions.explanation: Role, Context, Task, Constraints, Format.

questions.prompt: Which prompt element most directly reduces invented details in an underwriting summary?
options: "Use only the report text provided and write 'not stated' where information is missing"
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: A claims officer writes "Write a letter about a delayed claim." What is the main weakness?
options: No context, audience, reason for delay or constraints
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: Which constraint is most important in a delay message to a customer?
options: Do not promise a settlement date that has not been confirmed
questions.explanation: Unfounded promises create complaints and conduct risk.

questions.prompt: Why ask the model to ask clarifying questions before drafting?
options: It surfaces missing information before a draft is built on assumptions
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: Prompting well will make an AI tool:
options: Accurate about regulations it has never seen
Better at structure, tone and relevance, but still dependent on correct source information
Able to access the core system
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: A team reuses the same prompt for motor claim acknowledgements every day. Best practice is to:
options: Let each officer write their own each time
Approve, store and version a tested template
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: Which format instruction suits a WhatsApp update to a customer?
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: Giving the model an example of a good past message (with personal details removed) mainly helps it to:
options: Match the desired tone, length and structure
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: After receiving a first draft that is too formal, the best next step is to:
options: Start again with a new tool
Give a follow-up instruction such as "make it warmer and simpler, keep the same facts"
Rewrite the whole thing by hand without using the draft
questions.explanation: Iteration is part of prompting.

questions.prompt: An AI-drafted settlement letter shows UGX 4,850,000; the file shows UGX 4,580,000. Which check should catch this?

questions.prompt: What is the weakness of asking the same AI tool "Is this calculation correct?"
options: The tool may simply affirm its own output; it is not independent verification

questions.prompt: Automation bias is:
options: Bias in training data against certain groups
The tendency to accept machine output because it looks authoritative

questions.prompt: Which document needs the deepest verification?

A draft agenda for a team meeting
A list of possible training topics

questions.prompt: A summary for a corporate client omits the maternity waiting period. Which risk does this create?
options: Staff may rely on the summary and later dispute a declined claim

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports accountability for AI-assisted customer letters?

questions.prompt: An AI letter to a bereaved family uses a cheerful marketing tone. Which check catches this?
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to verify a clause reference an AI provided?

questions.prompt: Under heavy workload, a colleague proposes skipping checks on AI-drafted status messages. The best response is:

units.title: Protecting personal data when using AI

questions.prompt: Which body regulates the processing of personal data in Uganda?
options: Personal Data Protection Office under NITA-U
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: A claims officer wants an AI summary of a medical report. What is the best practice?
options: Paste the full report into any free tool
Remove name, ID and unneeded details, refer to "Patient A", and use an organisation-approved tool
Email the report to the AI provider
Ask the customer to summarise it

questions.prompt: Pseudonymisation means:
options: Replacing identifiers with codes such as "Claimant A"

questions.prompt: Why does using a public AI tool hosted abroad raise a DPPA issue?
options: The Act sets conditions for processing personal data outside Uganda
It does not raise any issue

questions.prompt: Who should decide which AI tools may process customer data?
options: The organisation, involving the data protection officer, based on contract and security terms

questions.prompt: A broker wants AI help with renewal reminders. Which approach applies data minimisation?

Share the client list on WhatsApp
Ask the AI to remember all clients

questions.prompt: Deleting an AI chat on a public tool:
options: Always removes the data from the provider's systems
May not remove data the provider has already retained, depending on its terms

questions.prompt: Using claims data to target customers with AI-generated marketing without a lawful basis conflicts with which principle?
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.prompt: The DPPA gives data subjects rights in relation to:

questions.prompt: Which statement about AI and Ugandan data protection law is most accurate?
options: The DPPA does not apply to AI
The DPPA applies to AI processing of personal data, though commentators argue it does not yet address algorithmic profiling in detail
AI tools are exempt if hosted abroad
questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

questions.explanation: Use the lesson's evidence and human-review principles.

What the agent may and may not do, and when it must hand over to a person

Giving an AI system more permissions or autonomy than its task requires

units.title: The governance landscape: IAIS, NIST, EU AI Act and Uganda

questions.prompt: What is the appropriate use of the IAIS AI application paper in this lesson?
options: A source of supervisory guidance to inform an evidence-based review
An automatic certification for an AI vendor
questions.explanation: Guidance informs the review but does not certify the system or replace applicable requirements.

questions.prompt: Who should own a consequential approval in the fictional summary pilot?
options: Whichever tool generated the most confident answer
questions.explanation: The review needs a responsible person and a recorded decision.

questions.prompt: Which NIST function establishes policies and responsibilities?
questions.explanation: Govern establishes organisational ownership and risk-management responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Which NIST function examines the use-case context and affected people?
questions.explanation: Map describes the context and relevant risks.

questions.prompt: Testing summaries against source documents primarily supports which function?
questions.explanation: Measure evaluates performance and risk using evidence.

questions.prompt: Responding to failed tests and deciding whether to stop supports which function?
questions.explanation: Manage prioritises and responds to assessed risks.

questions.prompt: A colleague cannot identify a familiar AI-specific law. What should follow?
options: Review the laws and requirements relevant to the actual activity and processing
questions.explanation: The technology label does not settle the legal obligations of the activity.

questions.prompt: How should an international legal applicability question be resolved?
options: Let the model infer the answer from a country name
Check current official sources and obtain an accountable applicability review
questions.explanation: Scope and dates need a current review tied to the actual facts.

questions.prompt: Does a completed governance form prove that controls work?
options: No; evidence and testing are still needed
Yes, if the vendor is well known
questions.explanation: A record of intended controls is not evidence of their actual operation.

questions.prompt: What belongs in the review when an important legal issue remains unresolved?
options: An omitted row so the review looks complete
The exact issue, assigned owner and next step before the affected action proceeds
questions.explanation: Keep the unresolved dependency visible and route it to an accountable owner.
